title: High-Throughput Optogenetics Experiments in Yeast Using the Automated Platform Lustro
protocol: Equip the automated workstation with a Robotic Gripper Arm (RGA).
Install a microplate heater shaker with an automatic plate locking mechanism that provides RGA access.
Position a microplate reader adjacent to the automated workstation ensuring RGA accessibility.
Incorporate a microplate illumination device allowing convenient RGA access.
Construct and calibrate the optoPlate following established methods.
Utilize an adaptor on the illumination device to enable RGA access.
Program the optoPlate using a spreadsheet input or a graphical interface.
Determine the desired light conditions for the experiment.
Enter the desired light conditions, including light intensity, start time, pulse length, number of pulses, and interpulse duration, into a spreadsheet.
Flash information onto the optoPlate using GitHub repository instructions.
Ensure sample plate is not illuminated while in the microplate reader or on the heater shaker.
Include dark conditions for each strain for background measurements.
Use high light intensity for initial characterization experiments to assess transformant functionality.
Optimize light intensity for sensitive experiments to avoid phototoxicity to yeast.
Configure the microplate reader to measure fluorescence from a reporter expressed by the strain of interest.
Cultivate the strain of interest in synthetic complete (SC) media to the highest cell density to be measured.
Transfer cultures into a glass-bottom black-walled microwell plate.
Measure cultures to determine optimal microplate reader settings.
Enter the plate dimensions correctly in the measurement script.
Perform a z-scan on wells containing fluorescent and nonfluorescent strains to determine the optimal z-value.
Conduct absorption and emission scans on fluorescent and nonfluorescent strains to optimize signal-to-noise ratio.
Set the optical gain for measuring the fluorescent strain at the highest level without causing overflow error.
Measure the optical density of cultures at 600 nm unless red fluorescent proteins are expressed, then measure at 700 nm.
Set the measurement script to maintain an internal incubation temperature of 30 °C during measurements.
Configure the measurement script to export data into a spreadsheet or ASCII files according to preference.
Configure the worktable definition in the automated workstation software based on the physical layout of carriers and labware.
Create a script in the automation workstation software to execute light induction and measurements.
Disable any internal illumination sources to prevent background activation of optogenetic systems.
Set the heater shaker to maintain a temperature of 30 °C.
Utilize loops, a timer, and a loop counting variable to repeat steps of inducing and measuring cells at regular intervals.
Shake the sample plate for 60 seconds at 1,000 rpm with a 2 mm orbital.
Move the sample plate to the microplate reader using the robot arm.
Remove the lid from the sample plate if applicable.
Execute the microplate reader measurement script as described in step 4.
Replace the lid on the sample plate after measurement.
Move the plate to the illumination device using the robot arm.
Set the script to wait until the timer reaches the specified time interval.
Repeat the entire loop for the desired number of iterations.
Run an empty plate through the script loop multiple times to troubleshoot potential errors and ensure proper functioning.
Configure user alerts to notify of any instrument state changes or errors during protocol execution.
Grow yeast strains on YPD agar plates.
Include a nonfluorescent control strain.
Inoculate selected colonies into 3 mL of SC media in glass culture tubes.
Incubate cultures overnight at 30 °C on a roller drum in the dark or under non-responsive light conditions.
Dilute 200 μL of each overnight culture into 1 mL of SC media for optical density measurement.
Measure the OD600 of diluted cultures using a spectrophotometer.
Dilute overnight cultures to an OD600 of 0.1 in glass culture tubes or microwell plates for high throughput testing.
Pipette diluted cultures into triplicate wells on a 96-well plate.
Include blank media and nonfluorescent cells as negative controls.
Incubate the plate at 30 °C with shaking for 5 h before light induction.
Place the sample plate onto the heater shaker.
Initiate the automation script as outlined.
Commence the light stimulation program once the initial measurement on the plate reader has been recorded.
Cover the automation workstation with a blackout curtain if not in a dark room.
Create a spreadsheet map for the experiment reflecting the 8 x 12 layout of the 96-well plate.
Include names of the strains being measured and descriptions of light conditions used in the grid.
Utilize a Python script or another preferred programming language to analyze the exported data.
Import the map spreadsheet into an array, associating strain names and condition names with each well of the plate.
Read the data from the exported experiment spreadsheet into another array.
Generate plots of the optical density values for each strain and condition over time.
Generate plots of the fluorescence values for each strain and condition over time.
Examine the optical density plots to determine stages of exponential growth or saturation in the cultures.
